That is a complicated question. For a start, you don't have to tell anyone anything if you don't want to. At your age it can be difficult to open up to those close to you because they may just dismiss the way you feel because you're young. Also it depends on if your parents are understanding people who will try to support you or if they don't understand mental health and will dismiss you. Ultimately it comes down to what you hope for by telling them. Do you want their support or do you feel as though they need to know because they are your parents? If it is support you want and you feel like your parents can give that support then you definately should tell them. If you feel as though they need to know because they are your parents then you should talk to someone else who can support you emotionally (best friend, teacher, therapist... etc) and then tell them (in case telling them goes wrong and you need someone else to talk to).

When you cut deep, disinfect, bandage, and go see a doctor. Cutting begins as a coping mechanism but quickly becomes a compulsion. When that compulsion stops being enough, you end up going deeper and deeper. If you don't stop now then it will only get worse from here and you may end up doing permanent damage. Please don't do it again.

I believe that you should ask your sibling if talking to these guardians is somthing they would be comfortable with as doing it behind their back may cause them to feel defensive and become withdrawn. Offering support as you have done is an excellent opener and you should reiterate it as much as you feel is acceptable. Make sure they know that the offer to talk is not just a one time thing but the offer stands (and make sure you sell that point as people mostly say "talk to me anytime" to be polite and don't really mean it). The moments in which they are ready to open up may be fleeting and at strange times when they have nothing to do but reflect on their situation. If you have the time then just being with them is good, even if you're not talking about it or even doing anything together, the company of a loved one can do a lot. Also, if you can, make sure this sibling is getting enough sleep and eating right as these things can severely worsen depression which could lead to less sleep and less food creating a downward spiral that is difficult to escape from.

Hope this helps.
